provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Joined fluency
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a full line without lifting the pen
The pupils should be able to maintain proper slope in their letters
Introduction:
Last term we learned to write letters one by one
Today we learn to join letters while writing
Content:
Joined fluency means writing letters without lifting the pen
Keep the slope the same for all letters
Practice writing joined letters on the board
Use your finger to trace joined letters in the air
Class activity:
Each pupil writes a joined line on their slate
Teacher walks around to help
Evaluation questions:
What is joined fluency
Show me how to write joined letters
Why do we keep the slope the same
Summary:
We practiced writing joined letters without lifting the pen
Good handwriting needs joined fluency and proper slope

topics.title: Paragraph copy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy a short paragraph
The pupils should be able to maintain proper margins and spacing
Introduction:
We can write single words and short sentences
Today we learn to copy a whole paragraph
Content:
A paragraph is many sentences about one idea
Leave space at the margin before writing
Use finger space between words
Write on every line of the paper
Class activity:
Teacher writes a short paragraph on the board
Pupils copy it in their exercise book
Evaluation questions:
What is a paragraph
Where do we leave space when copying
How many spaces between words
Summary:
We learned to copy paragraphs with proper spacing
Good paragraphs have margins and finger spaces

topics.title: Punctuation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify capital letters and full stops
The pupils should be able to use question marks and commas
Introduction:
We know letters make words and words make sentences
Today we learn special marks in sentences
Content:
Capital letters start names and sentences
Full stops end sentences
Question marks go after questions
Commas separate items in a list
Class activity:
Teacher reads sentences with punctuation marks
Pupubs hold up cards showing correct punctuation
Evaluation questions:
Which mark ends a sentence
When do we use question marks
What does a comma do in a list
Summary:
We learned about capital letters full stops question marks and commas
Punctuation helps us read sentences correctly

topics.title: Sentence building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make and write their own sentences
The pupils should be able to write about their best friend
Introduction:
We can copy sentences from the board
Today we learn to make our own sentences
Content:
A sentence has a subject and a verb
Start with capital letter and end with full stop
Think about your best friend
Write what they like to do
Class activity:
Each pupil thinks of one thing about their best friend
They share with the class and write the sentence
Evaluation questions:
What makes a good sentence
What do we start a sentence with
What do you like about your best friend
Summary:
We learned to build our own sentences
Writing about friends is fun and easy

topics.title: Short story writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write three sentences about their holiday
The pupils should be able to read their story aloud
Introduction:
 We can write single sentences
Today we learn to write a short story with many sentences
Content:
A story has a beginning middle and end
Write three sentences about your holiday
Read slowly and clearly when sharing
Use capital letters and full stops
Class activity:
Pupubs write three sentences about their holiday
They take turns reading their story to the class
Evaluation questions:
How many sentences in your story
What did you do on your holiday
Why do we read slowly when sharing
Summary:
We wrote three-sentence holiday stories
Reading aloud helps us share our stories

topics.title: Number words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write number words from one to twenty
The pupils should be able to match number words to numerals
Introduction:
We know numbers like 1 2 3
Today we learn to write numbers as words
Content:
Number words are how we say numbers
One to twenty are important number words
Write each word clearly with proper spelling
Match the word to the right numeral
Class activity:
Teacher shows number cards and pupils write the words
Pupubs play matching game with number words and numerals
Evaluation questions:
How do you write the number 5
What number word comes after ten
Match these number words to their numerals
Summary:
We learned to write number words from one to twenty
Matching words to numerals helps us understand numbers

topics.title: Address writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their house address neatly
The pupils should be able to memorize their address
Introduction:
 We need to know where we live
Today we learn to write our address properly
Content:
An address tells where you live
Write your house number and street name
Write your area and town
Keep each part on a new line
Class activity:
Each pupil copies their address from home into their book
They practice writing it neatly on special address cards
Evaluation questions:
What is your house number
What street do you live on
Why is it important to know your address
Summary:
We learned to write our addresses neatly
Knowing your address helps you stay safe

topics.title: Card writing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write inside a graduation card
The pupils should be able to write best wishes lines
Introduction:
 We give cards for special occasions
Today we learn to write messages in cards
Content:
Cards have messages for people
Write neatly inside the card
Use best wishes for graduation
Write your name at the end
Class activity:
Pupubs decorate graduation cards and write best wishes messages
They practice writing their names neatly on the cards
Evaluation questions:
What do we write inside a card
What does best wishes mean
Why do we write our name on cards
Summary:
We learned to write messages in graduation cards
Writing cards is a way to show we care

topics.title: Dictation practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write words and sentences from dictation
The pupils should be able to listen carefully to the teacher
Introduction:
 We can copy words and sentences
Today we learn to write what the teacher says
Content:
Dictation means writing what you hear
Listen carefully to each word
Write five words and one sentence
Check your spelling after writing
Class activity:
Teacher says five words and one sentence slowly
Pupubs write them down in their books
They exchange books to check each other's work
Evaluation questions:
What is dictation
How do we listen during dictation
Why do we check our work after dictation
Summary:
We practiced writing from dictation
Listening carefully helps us write correctly

topics.title: Revision and handwriting certificate
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their best page of handwriting
The pupils should be able to receive their handwriting certificate
Introduction:
 We learned many handwriting skills this term
Today we show our best handwriting and get awards
Content:
Revise all we learned about joined writing
Practice writing neatly with proper spacing and punctuation
Write your best page for the certificate
Be proud of your handwriting progress
Class activity:
Pupubs write their best page on special paper
Teacher gives handwriting certificates to each pupil
They clap for each other's achievement
Evaluation questions:
What is your favorite handwriting skill
What did you learn this term
Why is good handwriting important
Summary:
We showed our best handwriting and got certificates
Good handwriting helps us in all our school work
